name: Hard Lemonade With Mezcal

ingredients.name: lemon, at room temperature thinly sliced

instructions.primary_message: For the Pickle Lemonade: In a serving pitcher, place lemon slices. Add 1 cup sugar and use a muddler (or a wooden spoon) to mash sugar into lemon slices until all sugar is moistened. Let sit for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Add lemon juice, water, and pickle brine to serving pitcher, and whisk thoroughly until sugar has dissolved. Refrigerate until serving.
For Serving: Add mezcal to lemonade and stir to combine. Serve over ice, garnish with a pickle slice and a lemon round, if desired.

description: Pickle brine, lemon juice, and smoky mezcal combine in this marriage of pickle lemonade and hard lemonade that’s sharp, salty, and just sweet enough.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Dill pickles, thinly sliced lengthwise for serving (optional); Lemon slices for serving (optional); Soda water for serving (optional)

Notes: While I love the smoky flavor mezcal gives this lemonade, vodka, gin, tequila blanco, and even whiskey also work well if you want to spike the drink.
This recipe reflects my preferred balance of pickle brine, lemonade, and water for a sweet-tart drink. You can adjust the proportions with additional water, lemon juice, or pickle brine to suit your own taste, keeping in mind that the lemonade will dilute further when served over ice.

Make-ahead and storage: The lemonade can be refrigerated in an airtight container for a week, though I'd remove the lemon rounds after a day, as they can make the drink bitter.
author: Daniel Gritzer
